left.label: TELL THE TRUTH

image.subject: the Salem 1692 courtroom in the meetinghouse, judges at a raised bench in black robes, crowded benches, high rafters, townsfolk packed shoulder to shoulder below the bench, a clerk at a table writing the proceedings into a heavy ledger

storyboard.claim: They weren't struck by madness or bad bread; they were trapped in a new legal system.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same courtroom as 7, now the judge who wields the bargain.
storyboard.addedInformation: The confession is the court's currency.

storyboard.claim: The truth hanged you, and people responded rationally to those rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text only: the second half of the thesis.
storyboard.onScreenText: ...AND THE TRUTH HANGED YOU. THEY RESPONDED RATIONALLY.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the thesis begun in 9.
storyboard.addedInformation: People were rational actors, not lunatics.

storyboard.claim: They played the lethal game they were forced to play - the heart of Miller's The Crucible.

storyboard.onScreenText: THE LETHAL GAME - ARTHUR MILLER'S THE CRUCIBLE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same courtroom; the townsfolk now playing the court's rules.
storyboard.addedInformation: Accusation is the move that wins the game.

image.subject: a broad-shouldered Puritan farmer in his thirties, dark unruly hair and short beard, rough brown linen shirt with rolled sleeves and a leather work vest, Salem 1692, sitting alone on a plank bench in a dark stone-and-timber Salem jail cell at dawn, straw on the floor, a barred window, a small table with paper and quill, head bowed over his clasped hands, wrists chained

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the man shown in 12.
storyboard.addedInformation: The key idea of the analysis: the name.

image.subject: a broad-shouldered Puritan farmer in his thirties, dark unruly hair and short beard, rough brown linen shirt with rolled sleeves and a leather work vest, Salem 1692, seated at a small table in a dark stone-and-timber Salem jail cell at dawn, straw on the floor, a barred window, a small table with paper and quill, a quill pen poised above a paper and hesitating, while the periwigged judge, stands over him waiting

storyboard.claim: The question is what it means to put your name to a lie just to survive a corrupt system.

storyboard.claim: Did she break mentally under the threat of death and truly believe she was doing God's work?

left.label: SPARED
left.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, standing confidently with arms folded in a candlelit parlour

image.subject: a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, standing free at the parsonage doorway in morning light, watching a ragged, homeless middle-aged woman in a torn dark shawl and soiled skirts, tangled grey hair, Salem 1692, being led away down the muddy lane by a constable toward the jail

storyboard.addedInformation: Time jump and the coming warrant.

storyboard.concreteVisual: Cheever drawing the long needle out of the poppet's belly in close-up: the planted proof revealed.

storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the trick as a system-level weapon, not a one-off.

storyboard.addedInformation: The court's internal logic is collapsing even for its own expert.

image.subject: Mary Warren, a timid, mousy eighteen-year-old servant girl with light brown hair under a white cap, a plain brown wool dress and patched apron, Salem 1692, collapsing to her knees in tears at a wooden witness stand while stern black-robed magistrates on the high bench look down on her in a crowded Puritan courtroom

storyboard.concreteVisual: Mary breaking down on her knees under the magistrates' bench: the truth-teller crushed.

image.subject: Elizabeth Proctor, a composed Puritan wife in her thirties, brown hair hidden under a white linen coif, dark blue wool dress with a plain white collar and apron, restrained grave expression, Salem 1692, being led by a constable through a side door into a crowded courtroom toward the judge's bench

image.subject: Giles Corey, a wiry, weathered farmer in his eighties, white stubble beard and bald crown, patched brown farm coat and breeches, Salem 1692, standing upright in a grey field outside a timber jail with his chin raised and arms folded, facing a group of black-robed magistrates

left.label: SIGN AND LIVE

right.label: REFUSE AND HANG

storyboard.claim: Proctor's last choice: sign a lie and live, or refuse and hang.

image.subject: a broad-shouldered Puritan farmer in his thirties, dark unruly hair and short beard, rough brown linen shirt with rolled sleeves and a leather work vest, Salem 1692, seated at a small table in a dark stone-and-timber jail cell at dawn holding a signed sheet of paper, while the haggard young clergyman in black kneels on the straw and grips his forearm, pleading

storyboard.claim: Proctor signs, and a guilt-broken Hale begs him to lie and live.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same jail cell and same paper: the choice from 163 now has a voice pulling toward 'sign'.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: The same signed paper changes hands: from Proctor's private surrender to Danforth's public trophy.

storyboard.concreteVisual: Proctor ripping the signed paper in two — the paper that was going on the church door is destroyed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of the sequence: the paper signed in 162-164 and claimed by Danforth in 165 is torn apart.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: The words behind the act of 166 — why he tore it.

storyboard.concreteVisual: Elizabeth at the jail window turning away from Hale's outstretched hands while the cart waits outside — she will not pull John back.

storyboard.concreteVisual: Pregnant Elizabeth by the hearth with the children's boots and John's empty chair — the family his death will leave behind.

right.label: PURITAN LENS

storyboard.claim: Judging Proctor with a secular 21st-century lens misses what Elizabeth understands.

storyboard.addedInformation: States the Puritan scale of values plainly.

storyboard.addedInformation: Names the real target of the allegory.

storyboard.claim: Miller himself was called before the committee and refused to name names.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same hearing room as 177-178; now the lone witness is Miller, and he refuses.

left.label: PROCTOR, 1692

right.label: MILLER, 1956

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the critique sequence announced in 180.

image.subject: a row of plain weathered fieldstone markers in the tall grass of a New England hillside at grey dawn, a single white linen cap lying on one stone, bare trees behind, Massachusetts

storyboard.claim: Does the allegory rob the real victims of their truth? A vital critique.

storyboard.onScreenText: DOES IT ROB THEM OF THEIR TRUTH?

image.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, standing at a split-rail fence with his hand on a rolled land deed, gazing across ploughed fields toward a distant farmhouse, while behind him the periwigged judge, and the gaunt Puritan minister in black, stand together on the road

image.subject: an empty 1950s Broadway theatre stage under a single spotlight, a plain wooden Puritan chair at its centre, rows of red velvet seats in shadow

image.subject: the Salem 1692 courtroom in the meetinghouse, judges at a raised bench in black robes, crowded benches, high rafters, a stern grey-haired colonial judge in his sixties in a black judicial robe with white bands and a long powdered periwig, cold heavy-lidded eyes, Massachusetts 1692, sliding a land deed across the bench to a kneeling woman who has just signed a confession, while a court clerk stacks arrest warrants beside him, calm and orderly

storyboard.onScreenText: A SYSTEM THAT PAYS PEOPLE TO LIE WILL ALWAYS FIND LIARS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rule distilled from the courtroom machine of 185.
storyboard.addedInformation: The video's central lesson in one line.

image.subject: a broad-shouldered Puritan farmer in his thirties, dark unruly hair and short beard, rough brown linen shirt with rolled sleeves and a leather work vest, Salem 1692, standing alone and upright in a dark stone-and-timber jail cell at dawn, the torn halves of a signed paper on the straw at his feet, first light from the barred window falling on his face

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the lesson of 187 onto the viewer; starts the closing sequence.
